newsitem.title: USA: Roth, Moynihan plan Medicare commission.
newsitem.headline: Roth, Moynihan plan Medicare commission.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee chairman William Roth said Wednesday he hopes to introduce with Democratic Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, a proposal for a new bipartisan commission on the long-term future of Medicare.

Roth, speaking to a small group of reporters, said decisions had not yet been made on the size of the commission or its potential membership. The Delaware Republican said the purpose of the panel will be "to develop a bipartisan consensus as to what needs to be done."
Moynihan of New York is the senior Democrat on the Finance Committee which has jurisdiction over Medicare, taxes and some other entitlements.
Roth noted that if the Medicare problem were not solved, it would cost $500 billion in the year 2007.

President Clinton in his fiscal 1998 budget recommended cuts of $100 billion from Medicare over five years to protect the program's solvency for the next decade. But the program faces major problems early in the next century when the large baby-boom generation begins to retire.
